title: Frequency-addressed state-dependent operator composition
summary: This pass narrows the FANMC / NotSoSimpleNeuron thread to a stronger executable condition: an address must select resident structure, local persistent state must change the operator encountered by the next event, and A→B must differ from B→A after fast state has settled away. v0 isolates the mechanism in reduced resonators. v1 re-embodies it in heterogeneous quasi-active cable branches. v2 kills the strong 'cable length carries the spectral address' reading. v3 removes cable geometry entirely and shows a matched modal SSM can reproduce the gate. v4 then removes the supplied modal privilege: matched untrained dense Gaussian and orthogonal recurrences with persistent adaptation written in arbitrary visible unit coordinates fail to form a high-rank written-operator family. A same-fast-matrix rescue succeeds when slow write and feedback are aligned to the hidden modal coordinates. The surviving object is therefore not cable substrate or recurrence alone, but alignment between resident dynamical coordinates and the persistent state that rewrites the future operator. Older convergence is now explicit as well: DendriteAsIteratedFeedbackOperator already coupled frequency-selective physical dynamics to persistent operator write/replay; SelectCarryBindWriteAskSelect made stored medium directly become the later operator; GAx and ThirdWay treated computational identity as modal/continuation structure that credit must follow; and AnttisNeuron found basis reorientation more important than eigenvalue change in its strongest synthetic adaptive result. The present v4 result ties those older threads together by making alignment between resident dynamical coordinates and persistent rewrite the load-bearing object.

nodes.claim: Tests whether frequency can select resident modal/cable structure whose local persistent state rewrites the operator encountered by later packets, making addressed operator composition noncommutative after fast state has decayed.
nodes.survived: v0 passes a reduced-resonator gate; v1 re-embodies it in heterogeneous quasi-active cable branches; v2 shows kinetic heterogeneity carries the spectral address while morphology enriches the written-operator family; v3 removes geometry and reproduces the gate in a matched 96-real-state modal SSM. v4 sharpens the inductive bias: a dense system with the same 96-state budget and the same hidden fast matrix jumps from seed-0 address/operator ranks 2.367/1.719 with visible-unit adaptation to 3.039/3.051 when adaptation is aligned to hidden modal coordinates. Across eight seeds modal alignment keeps written-operator rank above 2.190 with median 2.475, while the same-fast-matrix visible-unit version stays below 1.720.
nodes.killed: Order dependence alone is insufficient; geometry-only systems can remain path-dependent while address rank collapses. v2 kills cable length as the load-bearing address, and v3 kills cable specificity under the current gate. v4 kills the weaker idea that any matched persistent dense recurrence naturally has the mechanism: Gaussian dense recurrence never exceeds 1.739 address rank or 1.246 written-operator rank across eight seeds; a long-lived orthogonal dense recurrence never exceeds 2.263 address rank or 1.648 operator rank. The unresolved boundary is learnability: v4 is untrained, so it does not show that a dense RNN cannot learn an internal basis aligning persistent adaptation with useful resident modes.

edges.why: The new repository takes FANMC's frequency-as-external-address result and asks the stricter question FANMC left open: whether the addressed event changes a resident operator so that later operator composition becomes order-dependent, rather than merely writing a persistent code.

NotSoSimpleNeuron established the receiver-side idea that resident active state changes what the next event encounters. This repository isolates that idea as an explicit noncommuting operator-composition gate and then re-embodies it in quasi-active cable branches.

InformationFlow made frequency and phase external coordinates for selecting interactions that write persistent routing state. The new experiment keeps frequency as an address but moves the consequence into a resident operator whose later composition is explicitly tested for order.

Operaattori supplies the structural-compiler view in which morphology generates an executable transport/nonlinear operator. The new repository studies the complementary runtime question: whether addressed local state can rewrite such an operator between events.

ArtificialCortex previously treated space, frequency and phase as coordinates of resident dynamical tissue. The new repository turns that broad architectural intuition into a much narrower controlled operator-composition experiment.

DendriteAsIteratedFeedbackOperator already closed a PURIFY -> COMMIT -> RETURN -> WRITE -> REPLAY loop in which frequency-dependent physical dynamics select a mode and local consequence persistently changes the operator encountered later. The current repository strips that older dendritic construction down to the coordinate-aligned operator-rewrite mechanism and tests noncommuting composition directly.

GAx treats computation as persistent modal families whose relative gain changes with context rather than as one averaged mechanism. The current repository supplies a complementary dynamical result: those resident computational coordinates become useful writable addresses only when persistent state is aligned with the modes being selected and rewritten.

ThirdWay makes computational identity a continuation that can move through coordinates and shows that delayed credit must be transported with that identity rather than left in stale coordinates. v4 reaches the same structural constraint from a different experiment: adaptation written in arbitrary visible coordinates fails, while adaptation aligned to resident modal coordinates restores the operator family.

AnttisNeuron Gate 5B found that most of its synthetic adaptive gain followed reorientation of the physical basis rather than eigenvalue/time-scale changes alone. The current repository sharpens that older clue by isolating basis alignment between resident dynamics and persistent rewrite as the causal difference in a same-fast-matrix control.

SelectCarryBindWriteAskSelect removes the transducer between stored field memory and later computation: the slow collision field itself changes a later cue trajectory. The current repository expresses the same abstract move without a fluid substrate, then adds explicit address rank, written-operator rank and noncommuting composition tests.

motifs.title: Addressing becomes computationally stronger when the first event rewrites the operator seen by the second
motifs.description: Frequency filtering, persistent memory and order dependence are each weaker than the combined object. The surviving condition is: different addresses excite different resident structure; the resulting persistent state causally changes the later operator; and compositions do not commute after fast transients vanish. v2 shows cable length is not enough; v3 shows cable substrate is not required; v4 shows generic dense recurrence is still not enough when persistent adaptation is written in arbitrary unit coordinates. A same-fast-matrix rescue recovers the operator family when slow write and feedback are aligned to resident modal coordinates. The current substrate-independent hypothesis is therefore coordinate alignment between useful resident dynamics and the state that rewrites them. The next boundary is whether learning can discover that alignment rather than having it supplied. The older genealogy now makes two precursor patterns explicit: persistent material can itself become the later operator, and learning/credit is most useful when it follows identifiable computational coordinates rather than arbitrary storage coordinates.

motifs.title: Persistent write must follow the coordinates of the computation it is meant to preserve or change
motifs.description: GAx keeps distinct computational families as modal structure instead of averaging them. ThirdWay then makes identity and delayed credit follow computational continuation rather than fixed coordinates. AnttisNeuron finds that basis reorientation carries most of its strongest adaptive synthetic effect. FrequencyAddressedState-dependentOperatorComposition v4 closes the loop with a same-fast-matrix control: visible-coordinate adaptation leaves a weak operator family, while modal-aligned adaptation restores high-rank addressed operator rewrite. These are different experiments, but together they isolate coordinate alignment as a recurring architectural object.

motifs.title: A persistent trace becomes stronger when it is the later operator, not merely a stored label
motifs.description: DendriteAsIteratedFeedbackOperator lets frequency-selected physical activity write the operator that will later be replayed. SelectCarryBindWriteAskSelect makes the stored slow fluid field directly alter a later cue trajectory. FrequencyAddressedState-dependentOperatorComposition removes the specific dendrite/fluid substrates and asks the common abstract question directly: does addressed persistent state causally rewrite the later operator, and do those rewritten operators compose in an order-dependent way after fast state has vanished?
